subject: Onboarding: offline release acceptance & transport playbook
messages:
From: Claire Liao <claire@globe-ship.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-22T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: onboarding question — physical delivery to air-gapped site

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the orientation call earlier. ACME Ops has an upcoming window the week of Jul 12 for receiving the site image and operator media. They asked for a concise acceptance checklist and the credentials we require at handoff (signing proof, manifest, operator contact). Can Redwood provide a one-page playbook we can hand off to their on-site engineer and the courier?

Key constraints:
- No external network during install (air-gapped)
- On-site operator is not a Redwood employee — only an on-site operator ID and physical signatures allowed
- They need to reconcile chain-of-custody paperwork with their security team

Can you send the playbook and confirm who will sign the bundle manifest?

Thanks,
Claire
Operations Coordinator, Global Logistics

Attachment: proposed-receipt-template.docx (referenced)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Claire Liao <claire@globe-ship.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-22T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: onboarding question — physical delivery to air-gapped site

Claire — thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a short playbook we can hand to the courier and the on-site operator. I copied Marissa and Hannah to fold in procurement and signoff steps.

High-level offline delivery playbook (summary):
1) Manifest & signing
   - Redwood will produce a signed bundle manifest (SHA256 digests + image version) and an accompanying detached signature file (signed-bundle-manifest.sig).
   - On delivery, the on-site operator and courier sign the chain-of-custody sheet. ACME should keep a scanned copy and provide the scan to Redwood via an out-of-band channel (SFTP/secure courier upload) after the install window.
2) Operator auth
   - Operator must present gov ID and operator ID issued by ACME. Redwood will provide an operator-handshake-checklist for the installer to confirm asset serials and bundle checksums.
3) Acceptance checks (pre-install)
   - Verify manifest digests against the signed manifest.
   - Confirm operator ID, courier seal numbers, and tamper-evident envelope integrity.
4) Install & verification (post-install)
   - Operator runs local verify tool (CLI) to validate bundle signature against the provided public key (we will ship the public key on a printed card inside the sealed envelope).
   - Operator emails a short acceptance statement to ops@acme-telecom.com and uploads chain-of-custody scan.

Deliverables Redwood will provide before the window:
- signed-bundle-manifest.sig (detached signature)
- acme-mtap_manifest.csv (manifest for inventory)
- operator-handshake-checklist.pdf (one-page checklist for on-site)
- Printed public-key card to include inside tamper-evident envelope

Next steps: Marissa — can procurement confirm lead time for printed cards and physical seals? Hannah — can security confirm the verify-tool CLI flags and whether the public key fingerprint should be included in the manifest?

Rishi
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — procurement notes:

- Tamper-evident seals: lead time 7 business days (we can source serialized seals tied to the manifest IDs).
- Printed public-key card: 3 business days to print & laminate; we will include a unique QR that points to the fingerprint only (no network content).
- Shipping crate: suggest double-seal with courier's tamper tape + serialized metal seal. Courier to note seal serials on the chain-of-custody form.

I've attached the operator-handshake-checklist.pdf and the provisional manifest (acme-mtap_manifest.csv) for review. Please check the manifest rows for device serials.

Procurement will prepare a single box containing: sealed USB media (image), printed public-key card, printed manifest, chain-of-custody forms, and seals. Courier instructions will explicitly state "do not open — deliver to named operator only".

Marissa Cole
Head of Field Ops, Redwood

Attachment: operator-handshake-checklist.pdf, acme-mtap_manifest.csv

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: claire@globe-ship.com
Date: 2026-06-24T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: onboarding question — physical delivery to air-gapped site

All — quick security notes and checklist updates from my side:

- Verify-tool: the CLI should accept --manifest <file> and --signature <sigfile>. It will compare the SHA256 entries in the manifest to the image and then check the detached signature with our key. If verification fails, operator must NOT proceed and must call the Redwood on-call (we'll provide a local number).
- Key distribution: printing the public-key fingerprint on the card is good. Also include a fingerprint on the courier packing slip so ACME security can independently confirm.
- Post-install telemetry: for air-gapped installs we require the operator to capture the local verification stdout into the acceptance form and include it in the scanned chain-of-custody upload.

I've added two rows to the handshake checklist: expected checksum field length and the recommended CLI command the operator should run (copy/pasteable).

Hannah Schmitt
Security Engineering Manager

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: claire@globe-ship.com
Date: 2026-06-24T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: onboarding question — physical delivery to air-gapped site (checklist + logistics)

Looping in logistics checklist from my side (ops readiness):

- Seal tracking: I will generate a simple tracking table we can attach to the manifest that enumerates seal IDs, USB serial number, courier waybill, and expected delivery slot (we'll post it to the Drive link).
- On-call escalation: Redwood will provide a 24/7 on-call number for the install window and a backup SAML-authenticated email address for receiving the chain-of-custody scan.
- Signatures: Redwood signs the manifest before shipping. Acceptance requires two signatures: on-site operator + courier. We will countersign digitally on receipt of the scanned forms.
- Dry-run: recommend a dry-run with ACME's local engineer one week prior (we can do a remote walkthrough using a mock sealed box).

I will post the seal-tracking table to the shared drive and attach the final signed manifest once printed.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Field Operations

Attachment: seal-tracking-template.xlsx
